column3: The Hebrew repeats “the land” for Jazer and Gilead and introduces the suitable region with “behold”; BSB joins the two lands and says “they saw.”
The Hebrew makes singular “the land” the subject suitable for livestock and says the LORD “struck” it; BSB carries the listed towns as plural subjects and says the LORD “conquered.”
The Hebrew says “in your eyes”; BSB uses “in your sight.”
The Hebrew names “the heart of the sons of Israel” as what is discouraged; BSB simply says “the Israelites.”
The Hebrew leaves the traveling subject unnamed and names “the heart of the sons of Israel”; BSB supplies “your fathers” and says “the Israelites” without the heart image.
The Hebrew ends with the reason for exclusion; BSB moves “Because they did not follow Me wholeheartedly” to the beginning.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name in “in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB replaces that occurrence with “His sight.”
The Hebrew ends with active “you will destroy all this people”; BSB says “you will be the cause of their destruction.”
The Hebrew uses unnamed “they” and “to him,” with a plain future building verb; BSB supplies the Gadites, Reubenites, and Moses, and adds “want to build.”
The Hebrew describes them as “clear” from the LORD and Israel; BSB supplies the explanatory phrase “free of obligation.”
The Hebrew says to do “what comes out of your mouth”; BSB says “what you have promised.”
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”
The Hebrew says the dependents will be “there”; BSB says “here.”
The Hebrew says they do not cross “armed”; BSB separates arming and crossing into two actions.
